title: Agentic Trading: When LLM Agents Meet Financial Markets
authors: Yihan Xia; Panpan You; Taotao Wang; Fang Liu; Han Qi; Xiaoxiao Wu; Shengli Zhang
key_contribution: Reviews 77 LLM trading-agent studies and highlights protocol incomparability, weak transaction-cost reporting, and poor reproducibility.
main_limitation: Survey lens rather than a validated final taxonomy; field still immature.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Core evidence for reproducibility and evaluation gap

title: AI Agents in Financial Markets: Architecture Applications and Systemic Implications
authors: Hui Gong
key_contribution: Proposes a four-layer architecture and Agentic Financial Market Model linking agent design to market outcomes.
main_limitation: More conceptual and systemic than implementation-driven.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Supports trust and governance framing

title: When Agents Trade: Live Multi-Market Trading Benchmark for LLM Agents
authors: Lingfei Qian; Xueqing Peng; Yan Wang; Vincent Jim Zhang; Huan He; Hanley Smith; Yi Han; Yueru He; Haohang Li; Yupeng Cao; Yangyang Yu; Alejandro Lopez-Lira; Peng Lu; Jian-Yun Nie; Guojun Xiong; Jimin Huang; Sophia Ananiadou
key_contribution: Introduces Agent Market Arena, a lifelong real-time benchmark across stocks and crypto with multiple agent architectures and model backbones.
main_limitation: Still early; benchmark coverage and real-world frictions need further validation.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Supports benchmark and continuous evaluation gap

title: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
authors: Yijia Xiao; Edward Sun; Di Luo; Wei Wang
key_contribution: Models a trading firm with role-specialized agents such as fundamental analyst sentiment analyst technical analyst trader bull/bear researchers and risk managers.
main_limitation: Performance claims require strict reproducibility and transaction-cost review.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Baseline for multi-agent financial workflow

title: FinRobot: An Open-Source AI Agent Platform for Financial Applications using Large Language Models
authors: Hongyang Yang; Boyu Zhang; Neng Wang; Cheng Guo; Xiaoli Zhang; Likun Lin; Junlin Wang; Tianyu Zhou; Mao Guan; Runjia Zhang; Christina Dan Wang
key_contribution: Introduces an open-source financial AI agent platform with Financial AI Agents, Financial LLM Algorithms, LLMOps/DataOps, and multi-source foundation model layers.
main_limitation: Platform contribution more than formal evaluation theory.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Useful infrastructure reference

title: FinMem: A Performance-Enhanced LLM Trading Agent with Layered Memory and Character Design
authors: Yangyang Yu; Haohang Li; Zhi Chen; Yuechen Jiang; Yang Li; Denghui Zhang; Rong Liu; Jordan W. Suchow; Khaldoun Khashanah
key_contribution: Introduces profiling, layered memory, and decision-making modules for financial trading agents.
main_limitation: Memory is trading-decision focused; broader thesis and macro memory remain underdeveloped.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Supports long-term memory research gap

title: ESMA / Alan Turing / ILB LLMs in Finance Report
authors: ESMA; Alan Turing Institute; ILB
key_contribution: Discusses responsible adoption of LLMs in finance.
main_limitation: Policy report rather than agent architecture paper.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Supports regulatory alignment gap

title: Finance Agent Benchmark: Benchmarking LLMs on Real-world Financial Research Tasks
authors: Antoine Bigeard; Langston Nashold; Rayan Krishnan; Shirley Wu
key_contribution: Builds a benchmark of 537 expert-authored finance research questions using SEC filings and an agentic tool harness with Google Search and EDGAR access.
main_limitation: Best model accuracy reported as below 50 percent, showing current limitations; benchmark is still mainly task-answering rather than full portfolio workflow.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Core evidence for real-world finance research task difficulty

title: Evaluation and Benchmarking Suite for Financial Large Language Models and Agents
authors: Shengyuan Lin; Kaiwen He; Jaisal Patel; Qinchuan Zhang; Chris Ding; James Tang; Keyi Wang; Yupeng Cao; Yan Wang; Kairong Xiao; Vincent Caldeira; Matt White; Xiao-Yang Liu Yanglet
key_contribution: Presents a suite covering the lifecycle of FinLLMs and FinAgents, including evaluation pipeline, governance framework, leaderboard, AgentOps framework, and documentation platform.
main_limitation: Very broad suite; investment-research-specific audit and thesis workflow still need refinement.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Important for evaluation lifecycle and governance framing

title: HedgeAgents: A Balanced-aware Multi-agent Financial Trading System
authors: Xiangyu Li; Yawen Zeng; Xiaofen Xing; Jin Xu; Xiangmin Xu
key_contribution: Introduces a fund manager plus hedging experts across asset classes to improve robustness during rapid declines and high volatility.
main_limitation: Reports very strong returns that require careful independent reproduction, cost treatment, and regime testing.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Good case for risk-aware multi-agent design and skepticism

title: FinRobot: AI Agent for Equity Research and Valuation with Large Language Models
authors: Tianyu Zhou; Pinqiao Wang; Yilin Wu; Hongyang Yang
key_contribution: Designs an equity research agent with Data-CoT, Concept-CoT, and Thesis-CoT agents for company analysis, valuation, risk assessment, and research report generation.
main_limitation: Needs stronger independent evaluation against professional analyst workflows and audit standards.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Highly relevant to shift from trading agents to investment research agents

title: FinGPT: Open-Source Financial Large Language Models
authors: Hongyang Yang; Xiao-Yang Liu; Christina Dan Wang
key_contribution: Presents an open-source data-centric financial LLM approach and emphasizes automatic data curation and lightweight adaptation.
main_limitation: Foundation-model level; not specifically an investment research agent framework.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Background for open financial LLM infrastructure

title: BloombergGPT: A Large Language Model for Finance
authors: Shijie Wu; Ozan Irsoy; Steven Lu; Vadim Dabravolski; Mark Dredze; Sebastian Gehrmann; Prabhanjan Kambadur; David Rosenberg; Gideon Mann
key_contribution: Introduces a 50B-parameter finance-specific LLM trained on a large mixed financial and general corpus and evaluated on finance tasks.
main_limitation: Proprietary model and data; not an agent system; limited reproducibility for external researchers.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Background for domain-specific finance LLM capability and data moat

title: From Deep Learning to LLMs: A survey of AI in Quantitative Investment
authors: Bokai Cao; Saizhuo Wang; Xinyi Lin; Xiaojun Wu; Haohan Zhang; Lionel M. Ni; Jian Guo
key_contribution: Maps AI in the quantitative investment pipeline from handcrafted alphas and deep learning to LLM-enabled agents and self-iterative workflows.
main_limitation: Quant-pipeline survey; does not fully solve auditability or investment-research-agent workflow.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Positions Project Aegis within quant investment evolution

title: Large Language Models in Finance: A Survey
authors: Yinheng Li; Shaofei Wang; Han Ding; Hang Chen
key_contribution: Surveys LLMs in finance and provides a decision framework for adoption under data, compute, and performance constraints.
main_limitation: Broader LLM adoption survey, not agentic investment research specific.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Background for finance LLM adoption and limitations

title: Large Language Model Agent: A Survey on Methodology Applications and Challenges
authors: Junyu Luo et al.
key_contribution: Provides methodology-centered taxonomy for LLM agents, including architecture, collaboration, evolution, evaluation, tools, and challenges.
